questions.q: What is the correct order of the five levels of leadership?
a: Position, Permission, Production, People Development, Pinnacle
Permission, Position, Production, Pinnacle, People Development
Position, Production, Permission, People Development, Pinnacle
Production, Position, Permission, People Development, Pinnacle
questions.why: The overview lists the ladder from position up to pinnacle.

questions.q: What does the summary say a management title really is?
a: A starting point rather than a goal
Proof that you deserve to lead
The main source of a leader's authority
A reward for years of hard work
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the title is where leadership begins, not what makes people follow.

questions.q: How do leaders earn permission to lead, according to the summary?
a: By making people feel valued and trusted
By defending their budget and headcount
By setting strict rules from day one
By outworking every member of the team
questions.why: Lesson 2: when employees feel cared for, trust follows and they grant permission.

questions.q: Why does the summary recommend developing other leaders?
a: It prevents bottlenecks and smooths future transitions
It lets you negotiate a bigger budget
It keeps salaries and turnover low
It makes your own promotion more likely
questions.why: Lesson 3 says shared leadership spreads the load and prepares a successor.

questions.q: What does the flock of geese image illustrate?
a: Leadership should rotate among prepared team members
Leaders should stay at the front at all times
Teams work best when each member flies alone
One strong leader is worth a whole flock
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes geese switching who leads the V formation.
